title: Rosanna Hashem killed by freak lightning strike in Sydney
text:
By Ashlea Knickel for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 01:34 GMT, February 9, 2025 | Updated: 01:55 GMT, February 9, 2025
The woman who died tragically after a strange ray caused a tree to break in southwest Sydney has been identified.
Rosanna Hashem, about 40, was fatally beaten when Lightning hit her property at Old Razorback RD in Cawdor around 5.30 pm on Saturday.
At that time, he was sitting out of his home, when the tragic incident occurred.
It had been perforated by the wood shrapnel when the lightning caused a tree to explode near where it had been sitting.
A friend was talking on her phone when she exploded in her hand due to the increase in energy caused by lightning, partially amputating her finger and fracturing her jaw.
He is recovering at the Liverpool hospital, where he is in a stable state.
“Both women had been seated about six meters from a large tree, and this had been beaten by lightning, which literally made the tree explode, sending debris everywhere,” said NSW ambulance inspector David Kynston.
“This is a very traumatic and tragic incident for the family involved, but also very confrontant for emergency services that attended, both knowing that young children had witnessed the incident as well as the injuries suffered by patients.”

Mrs. Hashem was the owner of Groomery Cat Grooming Services, a home -based business where the accident occurred.
Neighboring Rob Campisi said that the storm out of nowhere came out of nowhere and that it was different from everything he had experienced in the ten years he had lived in the area.
“It began to rain and, suddenly, the strongest blow we have heard,” Campisi told Daily Telegraph.
“The power went out and (I was) in the shed and … I looked outside and I saw a great cloud of smoke.”
Campisi said that climatic conditions did not seem bad enough to require staying inside.
“Sometimes you don’t know when your time is.”
